findings.where: "Where we're starting" section: the three destination cards (Canggu, Uluwatu, Kuta Lombok), each with a "Best hostels >" line, at desktop and phone
findings.fault: The cards look clickable but do nothing. Each has a white raised card, a hover rule, and a link-coloured "Best hostels" with a chevron, yet the parts map marks all three static. The hero's "Explore destinations" button and the nav's "Destinations" both lead here, so the page's main path to the guides ends at three cards that go nowhere.
findings.who_objects: The backpacker deciding where to stay. They tap "Best hostels" for Canggu, nothing happens, and they decide the site is broken or empty. The page's job of sending visitors to the destination guides fails.

findings.where: Nav "How we rank", footer "How we rank", and footer "Privacy", "Terms" and "Report content"
findings.fault: Each of these links points back to this same page. The ranking method is the page's own trust claim ("ranks hostels on merit alone"), and it can't be reached. Neither can the legal pages.
findings.who_objects: A visitor wary of yet another booking site, who clicks "How we rank" to check the merit claim and lands back at the top of the homepage. The claim reads as unbacked, and the dead legal links make the site look unfinished.

findings.where: Hero headline against the section heading "Where we're starting"
findings.fault: The hierarchy is inverted. "Where we're starting" is set about three times larger than the hero's heading and fills most of a screen, while the hero's h1 just repeats the MantaHostels wordmark that is already in the nav. After the logo, the eye lands on a section label, not on what the product does for the visitor.
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor scanning for what this is. The biggest thing on the page tells them nothing, and the promise ("rank on merit, book direct") sits in small body copy under a repeated logo.

findings.where: Destination cards: the place names and the "BALI" and "LOMBOK" eyebrows
findings.fault: The card titles and eyebrows are set in a monospace typewriter face. That is neither of the brand's two type families (Quicksand for headings, Nunito Sans for labels), and it looks like a font that failed to load or like code, not a beach destination.
findings.who_objects: The visitor and the founder. The cards look out of place against the rounded Quicksand around them and read as unfinished, which undercuts the "effortless" first feeling the brand promises.

findings.where: Destination cards: their border and shadow
findings.fault: Each card has a thick purple border and a heavy soft shadow at rest. Purple is not in the palette and has no job. The rules call for a thin sand border with no resting shadow. Together the border and shadow make the static cards look like the loudest controls on the page.
findings.who_objects: The founder, whose brand gives every colour one job and bars heavy shadows at rest. The visitor sees an off-brand, ad-like box that promises a click and gives none.

findings.where: Hero primary CTA "Email luc@mantahostels.com for launch news" (a mailto link), worst at phone, where it wraps to two lines
findings.fault: The one coral action is a full email address inside a long pill. Clicking it opens a blank email the visitor has to write themselves, with no word on what they get or how often. The label is long and wraps on the phone, and the pill shape departs from the 8px control radius the CTA is specified with.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker on their phone who might want launch news. Opening a mail app and writing an email to a stranger is high friction, so most won't, and the founder collects fewer contacts.

findings.fault: The secondary button has square corners and no fill on the turquoise, while the primary above it is a fully round pill. The two buttons look like they come from different systems, and neither matches the 8px control radius with a white ground that the rules set.
findings.who_objects: The founder, and a visitor who notices that the two side-by-side actions don't look like one product's controls.

findings.where: Nav links "Destinations" and "How we rank" at desktop
findings.fault: "How we rank" is underlined and "Destinations" is not, though both are plain nav links and neither is the current page. The difference looks like a current-page marker that isn't one.
findings.who_objects: An attentive visitor who reads the underline as "you are here" or as the only real link, and a founder whose rules keep one look per meaning.

findings.where: Footer tagline "piloting now in Bali" against the Kuta Lombok card
findings.fault: The footer says the pilot is in Bali only, but the destinations section lists a Lombok guide. The visitor can't tell whether Lombok is covered.
findings.who_objects: A traveller planning both islands, who wonders whether the Lombok guide is real. Small contradictions like this erode trust in a site that sells honesty.

findings.where: Whole page: who is behind it and proof
findings.fault: The page never says who runs the site or when it launches, and nothing shows it is current. The only trace of a person is a first-name email address. There is no proof of any kind (honestly none is held yet), and nothing stands in for it, such as the published ranking method or a launch date.
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor weighing whether to trust an unknown hostel ranker over the booking sites they know. With no person, date or working method page, they have little reason to sign up.
